dawn-0.text: Dawn, off Jacmel, August seventeen ninety-nine.
dawn-0.caption: Dawn, off Jacmel, August 1799.

dawn-6.text: The schooner Ferret lies still. Her sails hang empty.
dawn-6.caption: The schooner Ferret lies still. Her sails hang empty.

dawn-12_5.text: Far off, something floats on the sea.
dawn-12_5.caption: Far off, something floats on the sea.

dawn-17.text: A dead bullock. Sharks are feeding on it.
dawn-17.caption: A dead bullock. Sharks are feeding on it.

dawn-23.text: About six miles in shore lies the cutter Sparrow.
dawn-23.caption: About six miles in shore lies the cutter Sparrow.

dawn-29.text: Mister Fitton signals to her: come to breakfast!
dawn-29.caption: Mr Fitton signals to her: come to breakfast!

catch-0.text: Mister Fitton waits at the stern. The pork is on the hook.
catch-0.caption: Mr Fitton waits at the stern. The pork is on the hook.

catch-7_5.text: He lets the shark run. Sixty fathoms of line!
catch-7_5.caption: He lets the shark run. Sixty fathoms of line!

catch-14_5.text: Up it comes, over the side.
catch-14_5.caption: Up it comes, over the side.

catch-20_5.text: There it lies: the biggest shark of all.
catch-20_5.caption: There it lies: the biggest shark of all.

alongside-0.text: The papers lie drying on the hatch, one by one.
alongside-0.caption: The papers lie drying on the hatch, one by one.

alongside-5.text: Not a breath of wind. The sea is flat.
alongside-5.caption: Not a breath of wind. The sea is flat.

alongside-9_5.text: The lookout at the masthead calls down.
alongside-9_5.caption: The lookout at the masthead calls down.

alongside-12_5.text: The Sparrow cutter in shore, and her boat pulling on board.
alongside-12_5.caption: “...the Sparrow cutter in shore, and her boat pulling on board.”

alongside-18.text: Mister Wylie's men row on and on.
alongside-18.caption: Mr Wylie's men row on and on.

alongside-24.text: Breakfast waits below. The papers dry in the sun.
alongside-24.caption: Breakfast waits below. The papers dry in the sun.

alongside-29.text: The boat is alongside. What a long pull!
alongside-29.caption: The boat is alongside. What a long pull!

verdict-0.text: The Court of Vice-Admiralty, Kingston. November seventeen ninety-nine.
verdict-0.caption: The Court of Vice-Admiralty, Kingston. November 1799.

verdict-5_5.text: Both sets of papers lie on the green table.
verdict-5_5.caption: Both sets of papers lie on the green table.

verdict-10_5.text: The papers from the shark tell the truth.
verdict-10_5.caption: The papers from the shark tell the truth.

verdict-16.text: The clerk reads out what the court has decided.
verdict-16.caption: The clerk reads out what the court has decided.

verdict-21.text: The Nancy and her cargo are a lawful prize.
verdict-21.caption: The Nancy and her cargo are a lawful prize.

verdict-26.text: The judge sits over the court. His name is not known.
verdict-26.caption: The judge sits over the court. His name is not known.

verdict-30.text: Mister Fitton's shark jaws stand by the wall.
verdict-30.caption: Mr Fitton's shark jaws stand by the wall.

verdict-34.text: Lieutenant Fitton recommends these jaws for a collar for neutrals to swear through.
verdict-34.caption: “Lieut. Fitton recommends these jaws for a collar for neutrals to swear through.”
